## GTA 6's Map Has a Useful Feature I've Only Just Noticed

Open-world games of a massive scale often hide surprises in plain sight, and players continue to uncover intricate details long after their initial playthroughs. According to a recent report by gaming outlet Push Square, a player who has already logged over 300 hours in *GTA 6* has just stumbled upon a particularly useful feature built right into the game's map.

### Discovering Details After 300 Hours

Navigating the sprawling world of *GTA 6* requires spending a considerable amount of time staring at the in-game map, setting waypoints, and managing missions. Yet, even with more than 300 hours under their belt, this particular player admitted that a specific, highly useful map feature had entirely eluded them until now. It just goes to show how much depth and hidden utility Rockstar Games packs into its user interfaces.

### The Complexity of Open-World UI

Rockstar titles are legendary for their dense, feature-rich menus and map systems. Given the sheer scale of the environment and the multitude of interactive elements scattered across the map, it is entirely normal for certain functional design choices to blend into the background. Players often develop routine navigation habits early on, completely bypassing alternative tools or contextual shortcuts that could make traversing the world even easier.

### Editor's Take

It is always fascinating to see how open-world design can continue to surprise players hundreds of hours into a game. While finding a hidden map feature after 300 hours might feel a bit humbling, it highlights the incredible depth of detail Rockstar builds into its UI and environments, proving there is always something new to learn.
